newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM to start weekly Bologna cargo flights.
newsitem.headline: KLM to start weekly Bologna cargo flights.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV is to operate cargo flights from Amsterdam to Bologna during the summer in a bid to avoid weekend trucking bans in Italy, as well as in Switzerland and Austria, a spokesman told Reuters.
Due to start on June 28, the flights will operate each Saturday until August 2 in order to beat the ban that is aimed at reducing traffic congestion.
During the peak summer vacation period, Italy will stringently enforce its ban on trucks from 1900 local (1700 GMT) to midnight (2200 GMT) most Saturdays and all day Sundays.

A 100-tonne capacity Boeing 747-200 freighter wet-leased from U.S. carrier Atlas Air will operate the service to Bologna, a new destination for KLM. Wet-leasing covers the hire of aircraft and crew and usually also includes insurance and maintenance.
But as it was introducing a considerable amount of new capacity to Bologna, KLM said it had cancelled a weekly Amsterdam-Milan freighter service.
This has been operated on its behalf by UK-registered, Norwegian-owned HeavyLift Cargo Airlines with a 30-tonne capacity Shorts Belfast aircraft.
The spokesman said that the Italian airfreight industry had capacity problems at weekends because of the trucking ban and KLM Cargo was keen to operate a service for Italian shippers.
As well as Italy, there are weekend truck bans in Switzerland and Austria during the summer holiday period, providing further reasons for the Amsterdam-Bologna flights, KLM said.
KLM Cargo will operate weekday feeder trucking services from Bologna to Venice, Rome, Milan and Turin.

In Rome, a KLM spokesman said that due to the increasing importance of the Italian market, the carrier would consider operating a weekly Amsterdam-Bologna A300 Airbus freighter service from September.
